findings.title: totalPages off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
findings.body:
`totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, this reports one page too many. For example, 50 members with limit 50 shows "1/2".

Because `showingLast` compares `currentPage` to `totalPages`, the next button stays enabled. Clicking it sets `offset = min(offset+limit, user_count) = 50` and loads an empty page.

The fix is `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

findings.title: Public members endpoint accepts unbounded/negative limit and offset
findings.body:
`/groups/:id/members` is a public, non-admin endpoint. It now takes `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` with no clamping, and applies them to every group.

- Any visitor can pass `limit=10000000` and force serialization of every member of a huge group such as trust_level_0. The old code capped automatic groups at a default of 200.
- A negative `limit` or `offset` makes PostgreSQL raise "LIMIT/OFFSET must not be negative", which returns a 500.

Clamp `limit` to a sane maximum and floor both values at 0.

findings.title: Members endpoint response shape changed from array to object
findings.body:
`GET /groups/:name/members.json` used to return a JSON array of users. It now returns `{members: [...], meta: {...}}`.

This breaks any existing API consumers, plugins, or other client code that iterate the response as an array. The change is made without versioning or a compatibility path.

findings.title: Public group members page silently truncated to first 50 members
findings.body:
The public group route now calls `model.findMembers()`, which requests only `limit: 50` from offset 0. Previously, non-automatic groups returned all members.

The public `group/members.hbs` template has no pagination controls (next/previous exist only in the admin template). Any group with more than 50 members now shows just the first 50, with no way to see the rest.

findings.title: remove_member automatic-group test uses PUT instead of DELETE
findings.body:
The route for `remove_member` is `delete "members"`, but this spec calls `xhr :put, :remove_member`. Controller specs bypass verb routing, so the test does not reflect the real request.

It should use `:delete`, consistent with the other `remove_member` test.

findings.title: create ignores alias_level sent by the client
findings.body:
The admin form lets the admin choose an alias level, and `asJSON` sends `alias_level` on create. However, `create` only sets `name` and `visible`, so the chosen alias level is dropped for new groups.

The value only takes effect after a second save, which goes through `update`.
